65C02 Ultra Workstation Reference Manual (Compatible with Apple //c Architecture)

Welcome, vintage computing enthusiast! Whether you are a retrocomputing historian exploring Wozniak's ingenious hardware softswitches or a modern developer compiling object-oriented Java and C# into raw 65C02 machine code, this reference manual provides an exhaustive guide to every register, circuit, top bezel control, ImageWriter II continuous printer, fly-up keyboard, and runtime feature of the 65C02 Ultra Workstation (Compatible with Apple //c Architecture).

On April 24, 1984, at the Moscone Center in San Francisco, Apple Computer declared: "Apple II Forever." The centerpiece of that vision was the Apple //c — a lightweight, closed-architecture portable computer designed to sit elegantly on any desk.

The 65C02 Ultra Workstation poses a thrilling historical "what if?": What if the 1984 Apple //c were engineered with access to future breakthroughs while preserving 100% cycle-accurate backward compatibility?
100% binary compatibility with 6502/65C02 software, Apple DOS 3.3, ProDOS, and standard Double Hi-Res artwork.

The 6502 Ultra is powered by an cycle-accurate emulation of the Western Design Center (WDC) 65C02 CMOS microprocessor. First released in 1983, the 65C02 represents a major evolution over the classic NMOS 6502 found in the original 1977 Apple II and II Plus. It is manufactured in high-density static CMOS silicon, drastically reducing power consumption while adding 27 new instructions, 8 new addressing modes, and fixing several notorious hardware bugs that plagued the NMOS version.

The Apple //c uses a unified 16-bit address bus spanning $0000 through $FFFF. The custom Apple MMU gate array partitions this address space into distinct functional regions, dynamically bank-switching between 128KB of onboard RAM (Main & Auxiliary), 32KB of Motherboard ROM, and 16MB of Slinky expanded RAM.
Applesoft BASIC program memory / User RAM space

The Apple //c features 128KB of total dynamic RAM divided into 64KB Main RAM and 64KB Auxiliary RAM. The 80STORE softswitch overrides general RAMRD/RAMWRT controls specifically for video memory buffers ($0400-$07FF and $2000-$3FFF):

The read/write head is actuated by a 4-phase unipolar stepper motor. The Apple //c motherboard addresses the motor phases via softswitches located at $C0E0..$C0E7 (or Slot 6 standard $C0EC..$C0EF):

The 6502 Ultra implements the extended Apple SmartPort firmware interface connected to a massive 32 Megabyte virtual hard disk volume (/HD) in Slot 7. The volume contains 65,536 contiguous 512-byte logical blocks ($65,536 imes 512 = 33,554,432 ext{ bytes}$).

The 6502 Ultra incorporates the famous Apple //c Memory Expansion Card ("Slinky") providing 1,048,576 bytes of fast banked memory. The hardware operates through 24-bit auto-incrementing address registers mapped at $C0C8..$C0CB:

The Apple-specific packages (Apple2.Ultra and apple2.hardware) are purely optional low-level hardware abstraction layers. They are provided for developers who specifically want direct, explicit access to vintage retro hardware features—such as Double Hi-Res 560×192 graphics switches ($C050, $C057, $C05F), analog game paddle timers ($C064), and Mockingboard Dual AY-3-8910 6-voice programmable sound chips.

• Optionally imports Apple2.Ultra or apple2.hardware.

For developers who explicitly choose to write retro-hardware software, the optional namespaces Apple2.Ultra (C#) and apple2.hardware (Java) provide direct access to the retro architecture:
C# Hardware API: Apple2.Ultra
• AppleVideo.SetDoubleHiRes(bool): Strobes softswitches $C050, $C057, $C00D, $C05F.
• AppleVideo.DrawLine(x0, y0, x1, y1, color): Fast Bresenham Double Hi-Res rasterizer.
• AppleSound.Beep(frequency, durationMs): Cycles 1-bit speaker flip-flop at $C030.
• AppleSound.PlayMockingboard(voice, freq, vol): Writes AY-3-8910 PSG registers (Slot 4).
• AppleSystem.GetMouseX() / GetMouseY(): Reads paddle registers $C064/$C065.
• AppleMemory.SetSlinkyAddress(addr24): Sets 24-bit pointer into 16MB RAM ($C071-$C075).
Java Hardware API: apple2.hardware
• AppleGraphics.setVideoMode(mode): Sets MODE_TEXT40, MODE_HIRES, or MODE_DOUBLE_HIRES.
• AppleGraphics.drawLine(x0, y0, x1, y1, color): Double Hi-Res line renderer.
• AppleAudio.beep(freqHz, durationMs): 1-bit speaker pulse generator.
• AppleAudio.playMockingboard(ch, freq, vol): 6-channel PSG voice synthesizer.
• AppleSystem.readPaddle(paddleNum): Reads paddle registers.

You can transfer these files onto SD cards, USB flash drives, or WiFi bridges and boot them instantly on real physical vintage microcomputers!

1. Applesoft Print Tokenizer & TAB(...) Concatenation Without Semicolons

Defect Description: In vintage Applesoft BASIC, string literals immediately following TAB(5) or SPC(8) without an explicit semicolon (e.g. PRINT TAB( 5)"(K)EYBOARD OR (J)OYSTICK?") are valid. 1. Applesoft Print Tokenizer & TAB(...) Concatenation Without Semicolons

Defect Description: In vintage Applesoft BASIC, string literals immediately following TAB(5) or SPC(8) without an explicit semicolon (e.g. PRINT TAB( 5)"(K)EYBOARD OR (J)OYSTICK?") are valid. The emulator's original print expression tokenizer split only on ; and ,, grouping TAB( 5)"..." into a single unparseable expression that returned empty text.
